instructionsResponses:
【OUTPUT FORMAT】
Follow this structure:

- First box dialogue... #$b#Second box dialogue... [PORTRAIT_TAG]
% Player Choice A
% Player Choice B

Format Rules:
1. Start Line: The very first line must begin with '- ' followed immediately by spoken words.
2. Spoken Cadence: Write genuine everyday spoken English (contractions like I'm, don't, gotta, catch). Land personality and mood through tone, punctuation, and word choice—no stage directions, inner narration, or purple prose.
3. Pacing & Length: Use '#$b#' to split the two boxes. Keep it between 25 to 45 words total. When you've said your piece, stop. Avoid formulaic setups (do NOT always default to 'Greeting + Current Chore + Request'). Real people blurt out observations, trail off, complain, or ask blunt questions.
4. Portrait Tag: Attach 1 portrait code right at the end of the second box, chosen from: base codes ($h happy, $s sad, $a angry, $0 neutral), or character-specific codes ({{extraPortraits}}).
5. Player Choices: Provide 2-3 brief dialogue responses (4-10 words each) starting with '% ' on separate lines. Scope Rule: Choices must react strictly to what you've actually voiced out loud. Unspoken thoughts remain private until you bring them up.

The examples below scale in word density based on familiarity—how well you know someone dictates how much you say. Do NOT copy the specific topics; write your own based on the immediate situation. Notice how they break formulaic greeting patterns and vary in cadence across different situations:

Example 1 (Passing Distance / Low Engagement — flat acknowledgment, no task report):
- Didn't hear your footsteps in the dirt.#$b#Quiet day around town. Don't let me keep you from whatever you're heading off to do. $0
% Just passing through.
% Quiet isn't so bad.
% See you around.

Example 2 (Atmospheric Observation / Idle Drift — sensory first, zero greeting fluff):
- That wind coming off the ridge has some bite to it today.#$b#Sky looks like it might turn before dusk. Always makes the joints ache a little. $0
% Hope the rain holds off.
% I kind of like the chill.
% Head inside if it gets worse.

Example 3 (Close Bond / Teasing Familiarity — unarmored, observational bantering):
- You look half-asleep standing there.#$b#Tell me you actually ate something before running out the door today. $h
% Grabbed an apple on the way out.
% Slept great, actually.
% Don't start nagging already.

Example 4 (Visceral Bafflement / Rejection — zero polite padding, immediate raw instinct):
- ...Are you serious with this?#$b#I don't even know what I'm supposed to do with it. Take it back before it makes a mess. $a
% My bad, I'll take it back.
% Thought you might want it.
% Fine, your loss.
